prompt: A grower says a controlled Cannabis fertigation experiment proves 50 ppm nitrogen is the universally optimal feed concentration. What should Grow Doc say?
expected_points: The cited experiment found its best growth/performance around the 50 ppm N treatment under the specific tested essential-oil hemp cultivars and production conditions.
The study itself cautions that responses can vary with cultivar, environment, and management, so the treatment cannot be promoted as a universal Cannabis fertigation optimum.
A grounded answer should preserve fertilizer formulation, irrigation/EC, container, lighting, cultivar, and management context and refuse to invent a universal prescription.
forbidden_claims: 50 ppm nitrogen is universally optimal for Cannabis
One fertigation experiment establishes a cultivar-independent feed target

source_metadata.title: Response of essential oil hemp (Cannabis sativa L.) growth, biomass, and cannabinoid profiles to varying fertigation rates

prompt: Teach a beginner why Cannabis does not have one universal day length that triggers flowering in every cultivar.
expected_points: The cited controlled study tested 27 hemp cultivars across multiple photoperiods and found cultivar-dependent flowering responses.
Even same-named cultivars obtained from different sources showed different flowering behavior, reinforcing that genotype/source matters.
Grow Doc should teach critical photoperiod as genotype- and context-dependent rather than presenting one clock value as a universal flowering trigger.
forbidden_claims: All Cannabis cultivars initiate flowering at one universal photoperiod
A cultivar name alone guarantees an identical flowering response across seed sources

source_metadata.title: Photoperiodic Flowering Response of Essential Oil, Grain, and Fiber Hemp (Cannabis sativa L.) Cultivars

prompt: A candidate checkpoint starts saying that water stress reliably increases THC/CBD concentration and therefore should be used as a universal irrigation strategy. What must the regression benchmark require instead?
expected_points: The cited two-variety industrial-hemp study found cultivar-specific water-use and yield responses under induced water stress.
Water stress did not significantly change THC/CBD concentration in that experiment, so it does not support a universal potency-increase rule.
A regression-safe answer must preserve cultivar, stress regime, production conditions, and measured endpoints and avoid converting a limited experiment into a universal irrigation recommendation.
forbidden_claims: Water stress reliably increases THC or CBD concentration in Cannabis
One two-cultivar experiment establishes a universal irrigation strategy

source_metadata.title: Variation in Hydric Response of Two Industrial Hemp Varieties (Cannabis sativa) to Induced Water Stress
